title: fix(grounding): merge lag is not a release blocker — direction-aware freshness, hunch grounding, post-merge hook
context:
Two branches that each capture one record both regenerate the very same "N+1"
counts line in the grounding docs; the forge merges identical lines with no
conflict, the merged store holds N+2, and the committed CLAUDE.md is one behind
with no hook run and no human error. Every release-gate red of that class
(PR #128, #135, v1.26.2's first tagged run — fnd_c402046ac7) was this lag.

- src/core/groundingLag.ts: classify the committed block against the generated
  one. fresh (byte-equal) · lagging ( Touches invariant(s): con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file).
decision: The committed grounding block is checked direction-aware (src/core/groundingLag.ts): byte-equal is fresh; a difference confined to the counts sentence where no append-only count (decisions, bugs, constraints, components, policies) exceeds the store is LAG — records merged in behind the doc — reported as a diagnostic, never red; an append-only count ahead of the store (a record never committed) or any prose difference fails. `hunch grounding [--refresh|--json|--quiet]` gives the per-doc verdict and delta and regenerates from the PUBLIC store (HUNCH_PRIVATE_DIR pinned to an empty overlay); `hunch init` installs a post-merge hook that refreshes after a merge/pull that brought .hunch/ in, leaving the docs for the developer's next commit.
consequences: Adds dependency: node:test, node:assert/strict, node:fs, node:os, node:path, node:child_process.
alternatives_rejected: Regenerate grounding on main from CI and push a bot commit after every merge — rejected: a bot commit on the default branch behind a human's tag push still races the release, and it needs write permission the guard workflow deliberately lacks.

Drop the record counts from the grounding block so merges cannot drift it — rejected: the counts are the block's cheapest signal to an assistant, and the never-committed-record defect (fnd_6391b4242f) was only ever caught by them.
Tolerate any counts-only difference — rejected: a doc AHEAD of the store on an append-only kind means a record exists on a developer's machine and not in the repository; that must stay red.
Fix it only in the release gate (regenerate before `test`) — rejected: ordinary CI runs the same gate, so the freshness test would never fire anywhere and a genuinely stale doc would live forever.

evidence: synth:provider=deterministic, substance written by the agent that made the change
